title: FEI Tribunal Decision — FINAL DECISION C25-0033 ALDUWAYHI (2025 FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM)
text:
DECISION of the FEI TRIBUNAL
19 January 2026
In the matter of
Mr Nasser ALDHUWAYHI (APR; Ref. C25-0033)
(FEI Case number: 2025/FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM)
FEI Tribunal Hearing Panel: Ms Yuri Yagi (JPN)
FEI Tribunal Reference: C25-0033 [FEI 2025/ FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM]
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Saad ALQAHTANI/10262539/KSA
Horse/ID/NF: AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM/108CG12/KSA
Trainer/ID/NF: Nasser ALDHUWAYHI/10255516/KSA
Event/Date/ID: CEI1* 100 - Riyadh (KSA), 24-26.04, 2025_CI_0266_E_S_02
Date of sample collection: 26.04.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Flunixin
Bar Code No.: 1417795

I. Introduction
1. The Fédération Équestre Internationale (the FEI) alleges that Nasser ALDHUWAYHI
committed a violation of Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping & Controlled Medication
Rules – The Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers
in a Horse’s Sample. The FEI notified Mr ALDHUWAYHI of the alleged charge in his capacity
as the Additional Person Responsible.
2. Applicable Rules Provisions:
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List)
3. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
II. Factual background
4. Nasser ALDHUWAYHI (FEI ID 10255516) is a Saudi Trainer (the Additional Person
Responsible or the APR), who was the registered trainer of the horse Azzam Alshaytham
(the Horse), which competed, with its rider, Saad ALQAHTANI, in the CEI1* 100 – Riyadh
(KSA), held on 24-26 April 2025 (the Event).
5. The FEI (together with the APR, the Parties), is the sole IOC recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage, jumping, eventing, driving, endurance, vaulting, and para-
equestrian.
6. Blood samples were collected from the Horse on 26 April 2025. The Horse’s sample
returned a positive finding for Flunixin in its blood.
2

7. Flunixin is non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medication used to relieve pain, inflammation
and control fever. It is classified as a Controlled Medication Substance under the FEI
Equine Prohibited Substances List.
III. Procedural background
8. On 30 June 2025, the FEI informed the APR of a possible violation of Article 2.1 of the
ECM Rules (the Notification Letter).
9. The APR submitted his explanations by way of correspondences dated 9, 10 and 13 July
2025 to the FEI.
10. In accordance with Article 8.3.6 of the ECM Rules, if the Person Responsible and/or
member of the Support Personnel (where applicable) does not elect the Administrative
Procedure within the fixed time limit, the Administrative Sanctions shall be considered
declined and the case shall be submitted to the FEI Tribunal for final Decision.
11. In the present case, the APR did not elect the Administrative Procedure within the fixed
time limit. Therefore, on 10 October 2025, the FEI submitted its response and the case
file (the FEI’s Response) to the Tribunal for adjudication.
12. On 17 October 2025, the Tribunal Chair appointed a one-person Hearing Panel to decide
this case. The Parties were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the
Hearing Panel by 20 October 2025. In addition, the APR was invited to respond to the
FEI’s allegations by submitting a statement of defence and any supporting evidence by 6
November 2025. Finally, the Tribunal Chair informed the Parties of their right to request
a hearing by 10 November 2025, at the latest.
13. On 17 October 2025, both Parties confirmed having no objection to the constitution of
the Panel.
14. The APR did not file a submission or request a hearing despite having been notified the
Tribunal’s letter via email directly to him and through the Saudi NF.
15. On 12 November 2025, the Sole Panel Member acknowledged receipt of the Parties’
respective correspondences. The Sole Panel Member, noted that the APR confirmed
having no objection to the constitution of the Panel, but later did not submit any position
within the prescribed deadline. Accordingly, for the sake of good order and considering
that the APR was not represented by Counsel, the Sole Panel Member decided to grant
3

an exceptional and ultimate deadline to the APR to submit his reply to the FEI’s Response,
by 17 November 2025.
16. Again, the APR did not submit any position. Therefore, on 2 December 2025, the Sole
Panel Member noted the absence of position, and informed the parties that a Final
Decision, based on the file in its possession, will be notified to the Parties in due course.
17. In response to the Sole Panel Member’s 2 December 2025 letter, the APR indicated that
he had already answered “more than once” to the email sent.
IV. The Parties’ Submissions:1
A. Submissions by the APR
18. The APR elected to not submit any position in front of the Tribunal. His submissions in
front of the FEI can be summarised as follows:
18.1 On 9 July 2025, the APR submitted via e-mail that on 26 April 2025 following the
completion of the second loop, the Horse was administered Finadyne together
with half a litre of 50% glucose solution, saline, and Ringer’s solution allegedly as
an emergency measure due to its poor health condition caused by extreme heat.
According to the APR, thereafter, the Treating Veterinarian took over the
treatment and administered Dexamethasone and intravenous fluids.
18.2 Following question posed by the FEI, the APR admitted that he had personally
administered the substance, given the Horse’s health condition.
18.3 The APR justified the administration of the Prohibited Substance as a necessary
measure to safeguard the Horse’s life and welfare, after it collapsed due to
extreme heat (43°C) despite having passed the veterinary inspection. The APR
submitted that the treatment given to the Horse was a painkiller.
18.4 Despite the FEI’s response reminding that the presence of a Controlled
Medication Substance in a Horse’s sample without a valid Veterinary Form
constitutes a Controlled Medication Rule Violation, and further clarifying that
emergency treatments with Controlled Medication Substances are permitted
under the FEI Veterinary Regulations provided that they are administered by a
veterinarian and duly authorized through a retrospective Veterinary Form A
signed by the Veterinary Delegate/Veterinary Commission and the Ground Jury
1 The following section is a summary of the relevant facts and evidence of the Parties’ written submissions.
4

before the end of the Event, the APR neither provided further reply nor accepted
the Administrative Procedure.
B. Submissions by the FEI:
19. On 10 October 2025, the FEI submitted the FEI Response to the Tribunal. The FEI’s
position is summarised as follows:
19.1 Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules prohibits the presence of a Controlled Medication
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a horse's sample without a valid
Veterinary Form. The same article also provides that Support Personnel may be
regarded as “Additional Persons Responsible under this Article and Articles 2.2-2.5
ECM Rules where the circumstances so warrant”. As a strict liability offence, it is not
necessary that intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use be demonstrated in
order to establish an ECM Rule violation under Article 2.1.
19.2 In the present case, the analysis of the Sample confirmed the presence of
Flunixin in the Horse’s system. This finding alone satisfies the requirements of
Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
19.3 Article 118.3 of the GRs establishes that, “the Person Responsible shall be the
Athlete who rides […] the Horse during an Event […].” The PR is the Athlete who rode
the Horse at the Event.
19.4 The Preface to the EADCM Regulations specifies that 'in the discipline of
Endurance, the registered Trainer shall be considered as additional Person
Responsible and held additionally responsible for any violation(s) under Articles
2.1 of the EAD Rules and the ECM Rules.
19.5 This principle is further reflected in Article 118.3 of the FEI General Regulations
(the GRs), which establishes that “the Person Responsible shall be the Athlete who
rides, vaults or drives the Horse during an Event, but the Owner and other Support
Personnel including but not limited to grooms and veterinarians may be regarded as
additional Persons Responsible if they are present at the Event or have made a
relevant Decision about the Horse. In vaulting, the lunger shall be an additional
Person Responsible. In Endurance, the Trainer shall be the additional Person
Responsible.”
19.6 Accordingly, under the applicable rules, the Trainer in Endurance is expressly
designated as an Additional Person Responsible, alongside the Person
Responsible.
5

19.7 The FEI does not submit any request for the disqualification of the results
obtained by the PR and the Horse during the Event, since this was requested in
the procedure against the PR.
19.8 Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules provides that a Person Responsible with no previous
ECM Rule violation, but who violates Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, is subject to a
period of Ineligibility of six (6) months, unless he can rebut the presumption of Fault
on a balance of probability.
19.9 Therefore, in this case, to rebut the presumption of Fault, the APR must establish
to the satisfaction of the Tribunal (on a balance of probability), how the Flunixin
entered the Horse’s system. The APR must also demonstrate one of the following:
1. He bears No Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, i.e., that he did not
know or suspect, and could not reasonably have known or suspected even
with the exercise of utmost caution, that he had administered to the horse
(or the horse’s system otherwise contained) a Prohibited Substance. If
proven, the period of Ineligibility is eliminated completely pursuant to Article
10.5 of the ECM Rules.
2. He bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, in which
case, the period of Ineligibility may be reduced based on the degree of fault,
pursuant to Article 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
19.10 The ECM Rules stipulate, and the jurisprudence of the FEI Tribunal and the CAS is
very clear: It is a strict threshold requirement of any plea of No (or No Significant)
Fault or Negligence that the APR proves how the Prohibited Substance entered
into the Horse's system. In this context, the APR must provide clear and convincing
evidence that prove how the Flunixin entered the Horse’s body.
19.11 In this regard, the APR has expressly admitted that he personally administered
Flunixin (Finadyne/Fenadine) to the Horse on 26 April 2025 following the
completion of the second loop. The FEI therefore considers that the source of the
Adverse Analytical Finding has been established by the APR.
19.12 The starting point of any evaluation of the Fault / Negligence for the Rule Violation
is the “personal duty” of the APR following from Article 2.1.1 of the ECM Rules, i.e.,
his personal duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication Substance is present in
the Horse’s body during an Event without a valid Veterinary Form.” The definition
of Fault is provided for in Appendix 1 of the EADCM Rules.
6

19.13 To verify the APR’s explanations, the FEI contacted the President of the Treating
Veterinary Commission (the PTVC) at the Event, and who treated the Horse as per
the Veterinary Form A. The PTVC confirmed that when he reached the Horse, it was
found collapsed and lying down. However, the PTVC also confirmed that he
reached the Horse within less than two minutes of being notified, as the clinic was
located only 100 metres from the stables of the holding area. In addition, the PTVC
confirmed that, upon his inquiry, the APR initially denied the administration of any
medication prior to his (i.e., PTVC’s) arrival and reported that the Horse had
suddenly collapsed. Subsequently, the APR informed the PTVC that a spectator had
administered an injection which he later identified to be Flunixin, although the APR
had not been initially aware of this.
19.14 The FEI submitted that the APR expressly admitted to the FEI that he personally
administered the substance to the Horse, which contradicts the information
initially provided to the PTVC.
19.15 The FEI emphasize that this case concerns (i) an in-competition administration of a
Prohibited Substance without a valid Veterinary Form A and (ii) an administration
by a non-authorised person, which to the best knowledge of the FEI is not a
licensed veterinarian and/or does not hold the necessary and formal qualification
to be able to correctly and safely administer medication by injection.
19.16 In relation to point (i), the gravity of an unauthorized in-competition administration
of a Controlled Medication is significantly higher compared to an out-of-
competition administration, where the Horse might not have completely
eliminated the substance by the time of the competition, and may therefore test
positive as a result of a miscalculation of the Detection and/or Withdrawal Times
by the administering person. FEI Events are fully supported to carry out
(emergency) treatments of horses by authorized and qualified veterinarians, if the
need arises.
19.17 In relation to point (ii), it is extremely reckless and dangerous for a person without
the necessary qualifications to be injecting a horse. If done incorrectly, the horse
can sustain serious consequences and may even lose its life.
19.18 The sole justification advanced by the APR for the in-competition administration of
Flunixin (Finadyne) was the alleged need to safeguard the Horse’s health following
its collapse due to extreme heat. However, the FEI Veterinary Regulations expressly
provide for such emergency situations to be addressed through treatment by
accredited veterinarians and the subsequent submission of a retrospective
Veterinary Form A duly authorised by the Veterinary Delegate/Veterinary
7

Commission and the Ground Jury. In the present case, the PTVC who treated the
Horse confirmed that the clinic was only 100 meters away from where the Horse
had collapsed, and that he attended to the Horse within two minutes of being
notified of its collapse. Therefore, in the FEI’s opinion there was no reason
whatsoever for the unauthorized administration by the APR and the FEI does not
acknowledge the APR’s justifications.
19.19 In light of the applicable rules, the explanations put forward by the APR do not
justify the reduction of degree of Fault. Accordingly, the FEI finds that neither the
circumstances invoked by the APR warrant any mitigation of the applicable
sanction, nor can they support a finding of No Fault or Negligence, or No Significant
Fault or Negligence under the EADCM Regulations. As a consequence, the
presumption of Fault as stipulated in the Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules shall stand.
19.20 Article 10.4 of the ECM Rules provides that a greater period of ineligibility than the
standard sanction may be imposed if the FEI establishes, in an individual case
involving an ECM Rule violation under article 2.1, that Aggravating Circumstances
are present. The period of ineligibility shall be increased by an additional period of
Ineligibility of up to six (6) months depending on the seriousness of the violation,
unless the PR/APR can establish that they did not knowingly commit the ECM Rule
Violation.
19.21 The FEI submitted that the APR failed to provide truthful information to the PTVC
at the time of the incident. Furthermore, the administration of a Controlled
Medication substance to a Horse by a person who is not authorized to do so
constitutes a grave violation, and does not only breaches the VRs, but also causes
a significant risk to the Horse’s health and welfare.
19.22 In light of the above circumstances, the FEI is of the opinion that there are
aggravating factors, which justify an increase of the period of ineligibility to seven
(7) months in accordance with Article 10.4 of the ECM Rules.
19.23 The FEI respectfully requested that the Tribunal issue a decision:
(i) upholding the charge that the APR has violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules;
(ii) imposing a period of Ineligibility of seven (7) months on the APR, commencing
from the date of the Final Decision in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM
Rules;
(iii) fining the APR in the amount of 5’000 CHF;
(iv) ordering the APR to pay the legal costs of 2’000 CHF that the FEI has incurred in
these proceedings.
8

V. Legal Analysis
A. Jurisdiction
20. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, Article 8 of the ECM Rules and Article 18 of the IRs. The APR is a member
of the Saudi NF, which is a member of the FEI; therefore, the APR is bound by the ECM
Rules.
B. Legal Discussion
21. Although the Tribunal has fully considered all the facts, legal arguments and evidence in
the present proceedings, it refers only to the facts and evidence it considers necessary
to explain its reasoning in this decision.
i. The Burden of Proof
22. Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules states that sufficient proof of a violation is established by the
presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a horse’s sample. The Tribunal is satisfied
that the laboratory report on the Sample reflects that the analytical tests were performed
in an acceptable manner and that the findings are accurate. The Tribunal is further satisfied
that the test results evidence the presence of Flunixin in the Sample taken from the Horse
at the Event. Flunixin is a Controlled Medication Substance and the presence of this
substance in a horse’s system is prohibited at all times under Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
23. Pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules, the FEI bears the burden to establish all of the
elements of the ECM Rule violation to the comfortable satisfaction of the Tribunal. The
Tribunal notes that it is not in dispute that the FEI had successfully established that the
APR committed an ECM Rule violation. As a strict liability offence, it is not necessary to
prove intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use.
24. The burden of proof then shifts to the APR. The standard of proof for the APR to establish
how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system is by a balance of probability,
pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules. It is not disputed by the Parties that for the APR
to escape a six (6) month sanction, he must establish, on a balance of probability: (i) how
the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system; and that (ii) he bears No
(Significant) Fault or Negligence pursuant to Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
9

ii. Controlled Medication Rule Violation
25. As mentioned above, the violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules is not in dispute. The
analysis of the Samples revealed the presence of Flunixin in the Horse’s system, which
constitutes sufficient proof of the violation of Article 2.1. Therefore, the FEI satisfied its
burden to establish the ECM Rule violation and sufficiently proved the objective elements
of the violation pursuant to Article 3 of the ECM Rules.
iii. Length of the Period of Ineligibility and evaluation of Fault
26. Pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules, the period of Ineligibility for an Article 2.1
violation is six (6) months, subject to a potential reduction for No (or No Significant) Fault
or Negligence in accordance with Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules, or to an increase
of the Period of Ineligibility in cases of Aggravating Circumstances pursuant to Article 10.4
of the ECM Rules. To benefit from a reduction, the APR must establish as a threshold
requirement how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system.2
27. In the present case, the APR admitted having administered himself the Prohibited
Substance to the Horse. The Sole Panel Member is therefore satisfied that the APR
established, on a balance of probabilities, how the Prohibited Substance entered the
Horse’s system, which is moreover not disputed by the FEI.
28. Where this first hurdle has been met (i.e., establishing the source of the Prohibited
Substance), the Tribunal must continue with the second step and evaluate the APR’s
degree of Fault or Negligence.
29. The starting point of any evaluation is the “personal duty” of the APR, i.e., his personal
duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication Substance is present in the Horse’s body
during an Event without a valid Veterinary Form.” In this respect, it is necessary to look at
the definitions of Fault and Negligence, as defined in Appendix 1 of the EADCM
Regulations:
‘Fault. Fault is any breach of duty or any lack of care appropriate to a particular situation.
Factors to be taken into consideration in assessing an Person Responsible and/or member of
the Support Personnel’s and/or other Person’s degree of Fault include, for example, the Person
Responsible’s and/or member of the Support Personnel’s and/or other Person’s experience,
whether the Person Responsible and/or member of the Support Personnel and/or other Person
2 FEI Tribunal Decisions: C23-0031 [FEI 2023/FT12 – ALASOUF] dated 12 October 2023, C23-0034 [FEI 2023/CM05
– SAHM II] dated 8 September 2023, C23-0045 [FEI 2023/FT24 – DIFF LOOK] dated 2 November 2023, C23-0046
[2023/CM08 BALLON PARIS] dated 6 December 2023.
10

is a Minor, special considerations such as impairment, the degree of risk that should have been
perceived by the Person Responsible and/or member of the Support Personnel and/or other
Person and the level of care and investigation exercised by the Person Responsible and/or
member of the Support Personnel and/or other Person in relation to what should have been
the perceived level of risk. In assessing the Person Responsible’s and/or member of the Support
Personnel’s and/or other Person’s degree of Fault, the circumstances considered must be
specific and relevant to explain the Person Responsible’s and/or member of the Support
Personnel’s and/or other Person’s departure from the expected standard of behaviour. Thus,
for example, the fact that the Person Responsible would lose the opportunity to earn large
sums of money during a period of Ineligibility, or the fact that the Person Responsible only has
a short time left in their career, or the timing of the sporting calendar, would not be relevant
factors to be considered in reducing the period of Ineligibility under Articles 10.6.1 or 10.6.2’.
‘No Fault or Negligence. The Persons Responsible and/or members of the Support Personnel
and/or other Persons establishing that they did not know or suspect, and could not reasonably
have known or suspected even with the exercise of utmost caution, that they had administered
to the Horse, or the Horse’s system otherwise contained, a Banned or Controlled Medication
Substance or they had Used on the Horse, a Banned or Controlled Medication Method or
otherwise violated an EAD or ECM Rule. Except in the case of a Minor, for any violation of Article
2.1, the Athlete must also establish how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system’.
‘No Significant Fault or Negligence. The Person Responsible and/or member of the Support
Personnel establishing that their fault or negligence, when viewed in the totality of the
circumstances and taking into account the criteria for No Fault or Negligence, was not
significant in relationship to the EADCM Regulation violation. Except in the case of a Minor, for
any violation of Article 2.1 of the EAD Rules and Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, the Person
Responsible must also establish how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system’.
30. In the present matter, the Sole Panel Member notes that, while the APR admitted, in front
of the FEI, having administered himself the Prohibited Substance, he had initially denied
the administration of any medication prior to the PTVC’s arrival, and subsequently alleged
that it was a spectator who had administered an injection.
31. In front of the FEI, the APR justified the administration of the Prohibited Substance with
the need to safeguard the Horse’s health and safety following its collapse due to extreme
heat. However, as the PTVC indicated to the FEI, the clinic was only 100 meters away from
where the Horse had collapsed, and the PTVC arrived in less than two minutes after
having been called. Therefore, the Sole Panel Member agrees with the FEI that there was
no reason whatsoever for the unauthorized administration of the Prohibited Substance
by the APR.
11

32. Not only was it not justified, but what is more concerning is the fact that the APR
administered a Prohibited Substance to his Horse, as a non-authorized person, while –
to the best of the FEI’s knowledge, which has not been rebutted by the APR – the APR is
not a licensed veterinarian and/or does not hold the necessary and formal qualifications
to be able to correctly and safely administer medication by injection.
33. The Sole Panel Member further agrees with the FEI that the gravity of an unauthorized
in-competition administration is higher than an out-of-competition administration, where
the Horse might not have completely eliminated the substance by the time of the
competition, and may therefore test positive as a result, for instance, of a miscalculation
of the Detection and/or Withdrawal Times.
34. The fact that the APR proceeded to the administration himself is a clear aggravating
circumstance, since, as an unauthorized person, the injection could have sustained
serious consequences to the Horse, if done incorrectly.
35. Consequently, the Tribunal finds that the APR is not entitled to any reduction of the
otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
36. To the contrary, the Tribunal finds that the APR’s dangerous behaviour, amount to
aggravating factors which justify an increase of the Period of Ineligibility to be imposed
on the APR, of an overall seven (7) months, in accordance with Art. 10.4 of the ECM Rules.
iv. Sanctions
37. In view of the above considerations, the Tribunal finds that the applicable period of
Ineligibility is seven (7) months pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules which shall
commence on the date of notification of this decision.
38. The Tribunal also deems that the APR shall pay a fine of CHF 5,000 and pay CHF 2’000 to
the FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
VI. Terms of the Decision
39. As a result, the Panel makes the following decision and imposes the following sanctions
in accordance with Article 164.11 of the GRs and Article 10 of the ECM Rules:
a) Mr ALDHUWAYHI violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
12

b) Mr ALDHUWAYHI is suspended for a period of seven (7) months. The period of the
Ineligibility will be effective from the date of notification of this decision.
c) Mr ALDHUWAYHI is ordered to pay a fine of five thousand Swiss Francs (CHF 5,000).
d) Mr ALDHUWAYHI is ordered to pay two thousand Swiss francs (2’000 CHF) to the
FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
40. Mr ALDHUWAYHI, the Saudi NF and the FEI will be notified this Decision.
41. Mr ALDHUWAYHI may not, during the period of Ineligibility, participate in any capacity in
a Competition or activity that is authorised or organised by the FEI or any National
Federation or be present at an event (other than as a spectator) that is authorized or
organised by the FEI or any National Federation, or participate in any capacity in
Competitions authorised or organized by any international or national-level event
organisation (Article 10.13.1 of the ECM Rules).
42. If Mr ALDHUWAYHI violates any of the conditions in the previous paragraph during the
period of Ineligibility, the results of any such participation will be disqualified and a new
period of Ineligibility equal in length up to the original period of Ineligibility will be added
to the end of the original period of Ineligibility. In addition, further sanctions may be
imposed if appropriate (Article 10.13.3 of the ECM Rules).
43. According to Article 170 of the GRs, this Tribunal Decision is effective from the day of
written notification to the persons and bodies concerned.
VII. Legal Action
44. In accordance with Article 12 of the ECM Rules the Parties may appeal this Tribunal
Decision before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) within twenty-one (21) days of
the present notification.
FOR THE TRIBUNAL
________________________________________
Ms Yuri Yagi, Sole Panel Member
13

title: FEI Tribunal Decision — FINAL DECISION C25-0032 ALQAHTANI (2025 FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM)
text:
DECISION of the FEI TRIBUNAL
19 January 2026
In the matter of
Mr Saad ALQAHTANI (PR; Ref. C25-0032)
(FEI Case number: 2025/FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM)
FEI Tribunal Hearing Panel: Ms Yuri Yagi (JPN)
FEI Tribunal Reference: C25-0032 [FEI 2025/ FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM]
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Saad ALQAHTANI/10262539/KSA
Horse/ID/NF: AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM/108CG12/KSA
Trainer/ID/NF: Nasser ALDHUWAYHI/10255516/KSA
Event/Date/ID: CEI1* 100 - Riyadh (KSA), 24-26.04, 2025_CI_0266_E_S_02
Date of sample collection: 26.04.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Flunixin
Bar Code No.: 1417795

I. Introduction
1. The Fédération Équestre Internationale (the FEI) alleges that Saad ALQAHTANI committed
a violation of Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping & Controlled Medication Rules – The
Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s
Sample. The FEI notified Mr ALQATHANI of the alleged charge in his capacity as the Person
Responsible.
2. Applicable Rules Provisions:
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List)
3. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
II. Factual background
4. Saad ALQAHTANI (FEI ID 10262539) is a Saudi horse rider (the Person Responsible or the
PR), who competed in the CEI1* 100 – Riyadh (KSA), held on 24-26 April 2025 (the Event),
with his horse, Azzam Alshaytham (the Horse).
5. The FEI (together with the PR, the Parties), is the sole IOC recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage, jumping, eventing, driving, endurance, vaulting, and para-
equestrian.
6. Blood samples were collected from the Horse on 26 April 2025. The Horse’s sample
returned a positive finding for Flunixin in its blood.
2

7. Flunixin is non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medication used to relieve pain, inflammation
and control fever. It is classified as a Controlled Medication Substance under the FEI
Equine Prohibited Substances List.
III. Procedural background
8. On 30 June 2025, the FEI informed the PR of a possible violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM
Rules (the Notification Letter).
9. Despite numerous reminders sent by the FEI to the PR, the latter did not submit a
position nor did he request the analysis of the B Sample.
10. In accordance with Article 8.3.6 of the ECM Rules, if the Person Responsible and/or
member of the Support Personnel (where applicable) does not elect the Administrative
Procedure within the fixed time limit, the Administrative Sanctions shall be considered
declined and the case shall be submitted to the FEI Tribunal for final Decision.
11. On 10 October 2025, the FEI submitted its response and the case file (the FEI’s Response)
to the Tribunal for adjudication.
12. On 17 October 2025, the Tribunal Chair appointed a one-person Hearing Panel to decide
this case. The Parties were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the
Hearing Panel by 20 October 2025. In addition, the PR was invited to respond to the FEI’s
allegations by submitting a statement of defence and any supporting evidence by 6
November 2025. Finally, the Tribunal Chair informed the Parties of their right to request
a hearing by 10 November 2025, at the latest.
13. On 17 October 2025, the FEI confirmed having no objection to the constitution of the
Panel.
14. The PR did not file a submission or request a hearing despite having been notified the
Tribunal’s letter via email directly to him and through the Saudi NF.
15. On 11 November 2025, i.e. after the deadlines provided had already elapsed, the PR sent
an email asking why he had received the FEI’s email of 17 October 2025.
16. On 12 November 2025, the Sole Panel Member acknowledged receipt of the Parties’
respective correspondences. The Sole Panel Member, noting that there seemed to be
some interrogation in relation to the proceedings, referred the PR to the Tribunal’s and
the FEI’s previous correspondences sent to the PR in the context of the proceedings.
Furthermore, for the sake of good order and considering that the PR was not
3

represented by Counsel, the Sole Panel Member decided to grant an exceptional and
ultimate deadline to the PR to submit his reply to the FEI’s Response, by 17 November
2025.
17. Again, the PR did not submit any position. Therefore, on 2 December 2025, the Sole Panel
Member noted the absence of position, and informed the parties that a Final Decision,
based on the file in its possession, will be notified to the Parties in due course.
IV. The Parties’ Submissions:1
A. Submissions by the PR
18. The PR elected to not submit any position.
B. Submissions by the FEI:
19. On 10 October 2025, the FEI submitted the FEI Response to the Tribunal. The FEI’s
position is summarised as follows:
19.1 Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules prohibits the presence of a Controlled Medication
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a horse's sample. As a strict
liability offence, it is not necessary that intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use
be demonstrated in order to establish an ECM Rule violation under Article 2.1.
19.2 In the present case, the analysis of the Sample confirmed the presence of
Flunixin in the Horse’s system. This finding alone satisfies the requirements of
Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
19.3 Article 118.3 of the GRs establishes that, “the Person Responsible shall be the
Athlete who rides […] the Horse during an Event […].” The PR is the Athlete who rode
the Horse at the Event.
19.4 Article 9.1 of the ECM Rules establishes that an ECM Rule “in connection with a
Test in a given Competition automatically leads to the Disqualification of the result(s)
of the Person Responsible and Horse combination obtained in that Competition with
all resulting Consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and
prizes. […] Even if a Sanction is reduced or eliminated under Article 10 below, such
reduction or elimination does not reverse the automatic Disqualification of the
Result(s) mandated by this Article 9.“
1 The following section is a summary of the relevant facts and evidence of the Parties’ written submissions.
4

19.5 Article 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules also provides that, “an ECM Rule violation occurring
during or in connection with an Event shall, upon the Decision of the FEI Tribunal,
lead to Disqualification of all of the Person Responsible's results obtained in that
Event, with any and all Horses, with all Consequences, including forfeiture of all
medals, points and prizes […].”
19.6 To maintain a level playing field, the FEI requests the disqualification of all the
results obtained by the PR and the Horse during the Event, in accordance with
Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules.
19.7 Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules provides that a Person Responsible with no previous
ECM Rule violation, but who violates Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, is subject to a
period of Ineligibility of six (6) months, unless he can rebut the presumption of Fault
on a balance of probability.
19.8 Therefore, in this case, to rebut the presumption of Fault, the PR must establish to
the satisfaction of the Tribunal (on a balance of probability), how the Flunixin
entered the Horse’s system. The PR must also demonstrate one of the following:
1. He bears No Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, i.e., that he did not
know or suspect, and could not reasonably have known or suspected even
with the exercise of utmost caution, that he had administered to the horse
(or the horse’s system otherwise contained) a Prohibited Substance. If
proven, the period of Ineligibility is eliminated completely pursuant to Article
10.5 of the ECM Rules.
2. He bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, in which
case, the period of Ineligibility may be reduced based on the degree of fault,
pursuant to Article 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
19.9 The FEI submitted that the PR must provide clear and convincing evidence
that prove how the Flunixin entered the Horse’s body. In this regard, the PR
has not replied at all to the charges brought forward by the FEI. However,
based on the communications exchanged between the FEI and the APR, it
has been acknowledged through the APR’s own admission that the APR
personally administered Flunixin (Finadyne/Fenadine) to the Horse
allegedly as a first-aid measure in response to the Horse’s health condition
following the completion of the second loop in the Competition. The FEI
therefore overall considers that the source of the Adverse Analytical Finding
has been established. As to Fault/Negligence for the Rule Violation, the
5

starting point of any evaluation is the “personal duty” of the PR following
from Article 2.1.1 of the ECM Rules, i.e., his personal duty to ensure that “no
Controlled Medication Substance is present in the Horse’s body during an
Event without a valid Veterinary Form.” It is also the responsibility of the PR
to rebut the presumption of Fault and to submit all relevant arguments
regarding the source of the Prohibited Substance, as well as any allegations
that he or she bears No (Significant) Fault or Negligence in relation to its
presence. In the present case, the PR has failed to respond to the charges
brought forward by the FEI. Consequently, even if the FEI acknowledges the
source of the Flunixin, it remains impossible, under the applicable rules, to
evaluate the PR’s degree of Fault or Negligence, if any. Consequently, the
presumption of Fault as stipulated in the Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules shall
stand
19.10 The FEI also stated that no elimination or reduction of the period of Ineligibility in
this case is possible and the applicable sanction for the current violation should be
6 (six) months of Ineligibility in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules.
19.11 The FEI respectfully requested that the Tribunal issue a decision:
(i) upholding the charge that the PR has violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules;
(ii) imposing a period of Ineligibility of six (6) months on the PR, commencing from
the date of the Final Decision in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules;
(iii) disqualifying the result of the PR and Horse combination obtained in the Event,
and the consequent forfeiture of all medals, points, prize money, etc. won,
pursuant to Article 9 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules;
(iv) fining the PR in the amount of 3’500 CHF;
(v) ordering the PR to pay the legal costs of 2’000 CHF that the FEI has incurred in
these proceedings.
V. Legal Analysis
A. Jurisdiction
20. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, Article 8 of the ECM Rules and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member
of the Saudi NF, which is a member of the FEI; therefore, the PR is bound by the ECM
Rules.
6

B. Legal Discussion
21. Although the Tribunal has fully considered all the facts, legal arguments and evidence in
the present proceedings, it refers only to the facts and evidence it considers necessary
to explain its reasoning in this decision.
i. The Burden of Proof
22. Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules states that sufficient proof of a violation is established by the
presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a horse’s sample. The Tribunal is satisfied
that the laboratory report on the Sample reflects that the analytical tests were performed
in an acceptable manner and that the findings are accurate. The Tribunal is further satisfied
that the test results evidence the presence of Flunixin in the Sample taken from the Horse
at the Event. Flunixin is a Controlled Medication Substance and the presence of this
substance in a horse’s system is prohibited at all times under Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
23. Pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules, the FEI bears the burden to establish all of the
elements of the ECM Rule violation to the comfortable satisfaction of the Tribunal. The
Tribunal notes that it is not in dispute that the FEI had successfully established that the
PR committed an ECM Rule violation. As a strict liability offence, it is not necessary to
prove intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use.
24. The burden of proof then shifts to the PR. The standard of proof for the PR to establish
how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system is by a balance of probability,
pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules. It is not disputed by the Parties that for the PR
to escape a six (6) month sanction, he must establish, on a balance of probability: (i) how
the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system; and that (ii) he bears No
(Significant) Fault or Negligence pursuant to Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
ii. Controlled Medication Rule Violation
25. As mentioned above, the violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules is not in dispute. The
analysis of the Samples revealed the presence of Flunixin in the Horse’s system, which
constitutes sufficient proof of the violation of Article 2.1. Therefore, the FEI satisfied its
burden to establish the ECM Rule violation and sufficiently proved the objective elements
of the violation pursuant to Article 3 of the ECM Rules.
7

iii. Elimination or Reduction of the Period of Ineligibility
26. Pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules, the period of Ineligibility for an Article 2.1
violation is six (6) months, subject to a potential reduction for No (or No Significant) Fault
or Negligence in accordance with Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules. To benefit from
a reduction, the PR must establish as a threshold requirement how the Prohibited
Substance entered the Horse’s system.2
27. The PR chose not to participate in the proceedings (except for sending an unclear email
with no relevance to the case). Therefore, the Tribunal finds that the PR did not discharge
his burden of proving how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system.
However, based on the communications exchanged between the FEI and the APR, it has
been acknowledged through the APR’s own admission that the APR personally
administered Flunixin (Finadyne/Fenadine) to the Horse allegedly as a first-aid measure
in response to the Horse’s health condition following the completion of the second loop
in the Competition. The Tribunal therefore overall considers that the source of the
Adverse Analytical Finding has been established.
28. The starting point of any evaluation is the “personal duty” of the PR following from Article
2.1.1 of the ECM Rules, i.e., his personal duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication
Substance is present in the Horse’s body during an Event without a valid Veterinary
Form.” It is the responsibility of the PR to rebut the presumption of Fault and to submit
all relevant arguments regarding the source of the Prohibited Substance, as well as any
allegations that he or she bears No (Significant) Fault or Negligence in relation to its
presence. In the present case, the PR has failed to respond to the charges brought
forward by the FEI. Therefore, even if the Tribunal acknowledges the source of the
Flunixin, it remains impossible, under the applicable rules, to evaluate the PR’s degree of
Fault or Negligence, if any. Consequently, the Tribunal finds that the PR is not entitled to
any reduction of the otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles 10.5 or 10.6
of the ECM Rules.
iv. Sanctions
29. As the threshold of source has not been proven, the Tribunal finds that the applicable
period of Ineligibility is six (6) months pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules which
shall commence on the date of notification of this decision.
2 FEI Tribunal Decisions: C23-0031 [FEI 2023/FT12 – ALASOUF] dated 12 October 2023, C23-0034 [FEI 2023/CM05
– SAHM II] dated 8 September 2023, C23-0045 [FEI 2023/FT24 – DIFF LOOK] dated 2 November 2023, C23-0046
[2023/CM08 BALLON PARIS] dated 6 December 2023.
8

30. Pursuant to Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules, the results of the PR and the Horse
combination obtained in the entire Event are automatically disqualified, including
forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes.
31. The Tribunal also deems that the PR shall pay a fine of CHF 3,500 and pay CHF 2’000 to
the FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
VI. Terms of the Decision
32. As a result, the Panel makes the following decision and imposes the following sanctions
in accordance with Article 164.11 of the GRs and Article 10 of the ECM Rules:
a) Mr ALQAHTANI violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
b) Mr ALQAHTANI is suspended for a period of six (6) months. The period of the
Ineligibility will be effective from the date of notification of this decision.
c) Mr ALQAHTANI’s results at the Event with the Horse are disqualified, including the
forfeiture of any prize money, medals and ranking points.
d) Mr ALQAHTANI is ordered to pay a fine of three thousand five hundred Swiss Francs
(CHF 3,500).
e) Mr ALQAHTANI is ordered to pay two thousand Swiss francs (2’000 CHF) to the FEI
as contribution to its legal costs.
33. Mr ALQAHTANI, the Saudi NF and the FEI will be notified this Decision.
34. Mr ALQAHTANI may not, during the period of Ineligibility, participate in any capacity in a
Competition or activity that is authorised or organised by the FEI or any National
Federation or be present at an event (other than as a spectator) that is authorized or
organised by the FEI or any National Federation, or participate in any capacity in
Competitions authorised or organized by any international or national-level event
organisation (Article 10.13.1 of the ECM Rules).
35. If Mr ALQAHTANI violates any of the conditions in the previous paragraph during the
period of Ineligibility, the results of any such participation will be disqualified and a new
period of Ineligibility equal in length up to the original period of Ineligibility will be added
to the end of the original period of Ineligibility. In addition, further sanctions may be
imposed if appropriate (Article 10.13.3 of the ECM Rules).
9

36. According to Article 170 of the GRs, this Tribunal Decision is effective from the day of
written notification to the persons and bodies concerned.
VII. Legal Action
37. In accordance with Article 12 of the ECM Rules the Parties may appeal this Tribunal
Decision before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) within twenty-one (21) days of
the present notification.
FOR THE TRIBUNAL
________________________________________
Ms Yuri Yagi, Sole Panel Member
10

title: FEI Tribunal Decision — FEI Tribunal Decision Settlement Agreement Case C25-0019 2025BS04 FELLOW VAN'T MOERVEN VALLEJO PR
text:
DECISION RENDERED BY FEI TRIBUNAL
19 December 2025
in the matter of
Mr. Arturo Parada Vallejo – Person Responsible (the “PR”) (Ref. C25-0019)
(FEI Case number: 2025/BS04) FELLOW VAN'T MOERVEN
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Ms Diane Pitts, (USA), Sole Panel Member (the “Panel”)
FEI Tribunal reference: C25-0019 PARADA
Horse/Passport: FELLOW VAN'T MOERVEN /106CI24/MEX
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Arturo PARADA VALLEJO/ 10095117/MEX
Event/Date: CSIO4* - Wellington, FL, Equestrian Center (USA), 25.02.2025-02.03.2025
Event/ID: 2025_CI_0407_S_S_01
Date of sample collection: 02.03.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Lamotrigine
Bar Code No.: 1488305
1

I. INTRODUCTION
1. This Decision pertains to the FEI case (2025/BS04) (FELLOW VAN'T MOERVEN) (the “Horse”).
In respect of this case, the FEI notified the PR of a violation of Article 2.1 (The presence of a
Banned Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample) of the Equine Anti-
doping Rules (the “EADRs”) based on the Laboratory's Adverse Analytical Finding (the “AAF”)
of Lamotrigine in the Horse's Sample collected at the CSIO4* - Wellington, FL, Equestrian
Center (USA), 25.02.2025-02.03.2025 (the “Event”).
2. A Settlement Agreement between the FEI and the PR was agreed by the Parties on 10
November 2025 (the “Settlement Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement and the Exhibits
thereto are hereby incorporated herein by reference.
II. Applicable Rule Provisions:
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, 1 January 2020, updates effective 1 January
2025 (“GRs”).
▪ Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations, 4th edition, effective
1 January 2025 (“EADCMRs”). The EADCM Rules are divided into the Equine Anti-
Doping Rules (the “EADRs”) and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the
“ECM Rules”).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 3rd Edition, 1 February 2025 (“the IRs”).
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21st November 2023 (the “Statutes”).
III. PARTIES
3. Mr. Arturo PARADA VALLEJO (FEI ID 10095117), the PR in accordance with Article 118.3
of the GRs, is an Athlete in the discipline of Jumping for Mexico (the “MEX-NF”), who
competed with the Horse at the Event.
4. The FEI is the IOC-recognised international governing body for the equestrian sport
disciplines of Dressage and Para-Dressage, Jumping, Eventing, Driving and Para-Driving,
Endurance and Vaulting.
2

IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND
5. The Horse was tested during the Event, and the analysis of the urine and blood samples
revealed the presence of Lamotrigine, an anticonvulsant used to control seizures and
mood changes in bipolar disorder. Lamotrigine is classified as a Banned Substance
under the 2025 FEI Equine Prohibited Substances List (the “List”).
6. By Notification Letter dated 22 April 2025 (the “Notification Letter”), the FEI informed the
PR of a potential violation of Article 2.1 of the EADRs, the Presence of a Banned Substance
and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample based on the findings of
Lamotrigine in the samples. The PR was also notified in said letter that he was
provisionally suspended under Article 7.4.1 of the EADRs, and the Horse was also
provisionally suspended for two months until 21 June 2025.
7. The Notification Letter also outlined the following options to the PR that:
• within 10 days of the Notification Letter, he may request the B sample analysis;
• within 20 days of the Notification Letter, he may admit the violation and receive an
automatic six (6) month reduction in the Period of Ineligibility;
• alternatively, within 20 days of the Notification Letter, he may challenge the violation
and/or consequences;
• that he has the right to a Preliminary Hearing;
• that he may enter into a case resolution agreement with the FEI;
• that he has the option to provide substantial assistance;
• that he may ask for the automatic disqualification of his results.
8. By letter dated 29 April 2025, the PR requested for the B Sample to be analysed. The
urine and blood samples (Sample no 1488305) were sent to the FEI-approved Hong Kong
Jockey Club Racing Laboratory (the “Laboratory”) in Sha Tin, NT (HKG), for analysis. The B
Sample analysis of the urine and blood sample confirmed the presence of Lamotrigine.
The PR was notified of the results of the B Sample analysis by letter dated 26 May 2025.
9. The PR submitted that the Lamotrigine detected in the Horse’s sample on 2 March 2025,
more likely than not came from the inadvertent transfer of Lamotrigine residue from a
colleague of his cousin, who attended the Event and helped with the horse on the day in
question. The colleague inadvertently transferred the substance when he broke the
Lamotrigine medication in his hands to ingest it (which he took to treat his post-accident
seizures). The FEI expert confirmed that such explanation was scientifically plausible.
3

10. On 11 June 2025, the PR requested the urgent lifting of the provisional suspension in
accordance with Article 7.4.4 (ii) of the EADR. The FEI consented to that request and
confirmed that the parties were currently in negotiations to enter into a no-fault
agreement.
11. On 14 June 2025, the Panel issued the Operative Award and lifted the provisional
suspension with effect from midnight CET.
12. On 13 November 2025, the FEI submitted the Settlement Agreement with Exhibits for
the approval of the FEI Tribunal (the “Tribunal”) and requested for a FEI Tribunal Panel
to be appointed for the purpose or review and approval of said Settlement Agreement.
13. On 5 December 2025, the Tribunal informed the Parties of the appointment of a sole
panel member (the “Panel”) to adjudicate and approve this case. The Parties were
asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the Panel by 9 December 2025.
On 8 and 9 December 2025, the FEI and PR, respectively, provided no objections to
the constitution of the Panel.
V. ACCEPTED TERMS
14. The Settlement Agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs and is
subject to the approval of the Tribunal.
NOW, THEREFORE, THE PARTIES HAVE AGREED TO THE FOLLOWING
TERMS FOR THE CLOSURE OF THE PROCEEDINGS:
15. In the matter of the Adverse Analytical Finding related to the samples, which were collected
from the PR’s horse FELLOW VAN’T MOERVEN in the CSIO4*-L in Wellington, FL (USA),
between 25 February and 2 March 2025, the PR and the FEI agree in accordance with the
Article 10.8.2 of the EADR on the following:
(a) The PR admits the violation of Article 2.1 EADR (The presence of a Banned Substance
and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample);
(b) The PR established, on a balance of probabilities, how Lamotrigine entered the Horse’s
system;
4

(c) The PR has established that he bore No Fault or Negligence for the rule violation in
accordance with the Article 10.5 EADR;
(d) The period of Ineligibility imposed on the PR shall therefore be eliminated;
(e) The results achieved by the PR and the Horse at the Event are disqualified, with all
resulting consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes, in
accordance with the Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the EADR;
(f) The PR’s Horse was Provisionally Suspended for the period of two (2) months (until 21
June 2025);
(g) The PR shall not incur any fine;
(h) Each party will bear its own legal and other costs incurred in connection with these
proceedings;
(i) No other Sanctions will apply in this case;
(j) In accordance with Article 10.9.2 of the EADR, this violation of the EADR shall not be
considered a prior violation for the purpose of Article 10.9 (Multiple Violations) of the
EADR.
16. This agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR and is subject
to the approval of the FEI Tribunal. The Parties hereby kindly request that the FEI
Tribunal issue a Decision incorporating the terms of this agreement.
17. In accordance with the Article 10.8.2 of the EADR, the Decision by the FEI to enter or not
enter into a case resolution agreement, and the amount of the reduction to, and the starting
date of, the period of Ineligibility and the confirmation of the case resolution agreement by
the FEI Tribunal are not subject to appeal under Article 13 of the EADR.
18. The parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADR, the Decision
will be made public by the FEI.
19. The terms set out in this agreement have been agreed as a full and final settlement of all
claims relating to the subject-matter of these proceedings. Accordingly, any and all other
claims for relief that any party might otherwise have made against another in relation to the
subject matter of these proceedings are released and discharged unconditionally, and they
may not be pursued in any form hereafter.
VI. DECISION
1. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
159 of the GRs, the EADRs and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member of the MEX-NF,
5

which is a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the EADRs.
2. Having reviewed the case summary, the full reasoning of the Settlement Agreement and
the Accepted Terms, the Hearing Panel accepts that the FEI found that the PR had
established, on a balance of probabilities, how Lamotrigine entered the Horse’s system.
3. The Tribunal further acknowledges that the PR and the FEI have agreed on the terms for
the closure of the proceedings, in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs, as detailed
under Section V of this Decision.
4. The Tribunal confirms that the Accepted Terms of the Settlement Agreement comply with
the EADRs and finds no grounds to object thereto.
5. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADRs this Final
Decision will be made public by the FEI. The terms set out in the Settlement Agreement
are a full and final settlement of all claims relating to the subject matter of these
proceedings.
6. The Settlement Agreement and this Decision are not subject to appeal under Article 13
of the EADRs.
DECISION TO BE FORWARDED TO:
a. The Parties: Yes
b. The NF of the PR: Yes
c. Any other: No

Ms Diane Pitts (USA), Sole Panel Member

title: FEI Tribunal Decision — FEI Tribunal Final Decision Settlement Agreement Case 2025 BS07 (2025ATF02) CASTLEFIELD CORNELIOUS Ms CAMPBELL C25-0027-Corr
text:
DECISION RENDERED BY FEI TRIBUNAL
11 November 2025
in the matter of
Ms Kaitlin CAMPBELL (the “PR”) (Ref. C25-0027)
(FEI Case number: 2025/BS07 - 2025/ATF02) CASTLEFIELD CORNELIOUS
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Mr Agustin Fattal Jaef, (ARG), Sole Panel Member
Ref. no. FEI Tribunal: C25-0027 CAMPBELL (2025/BS07(2025/ATF02) CASTLEFIELD
CORNELIOUS)
Horse/Passport: CASTLEFIELD CORNELIOUS/105KI20/USA
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Kaitlin CAMPBELL/10060519/USA
Event/Date: CSI5* MLSJ - Thermal CA (USA), 04-07.12.2024
Event Code: 2024_CI_0253_S_S_01
Date of sample collection: 07.12.2024
Prohibited Substance(s): Octopamine, Dexamethasone
Bar Code Nos.: 1489271
1

I. INTRODUCTION
1. This Decision pertains to the FEI case (2025/BS07(2025/ATF02) CASTLEFIELD CORNELIOUS)
(the “Horse”). In respect of this case, the FEI notified the PR that a violation of Article 2.1 (the
Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a
Horse’s Sample) and Article 2.2 (the Use of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or
Controlled Medication Method) of the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (“ECMRs”) and
Article 2.1 (The Presence of a Banned Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a
Horse’s Sample) and Article 2.2 (the Use of a Banned Substance and/or Banned Method) of
the Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the “EADRs”) had occurred based on the adverse analytical
findings (the “AAFs”) of Synephrine, Octopamine and Dexamethasone in the Horse’s sample.
2. The positive findings of Octopamine and Dexamethasone in the Horse’s sample gave rise to
an Anti-Doping Rule Violation under Article 2.1 and Article 2.2 of the EADCMRs collected at
the CSI5* MLSJ - Thermal CA (USA), 04-07.12.2024 (the “Event”).
3. A Settlement Agreement between the FEI and the PR was agreed by the Parties on 19
September 2025 (the “Settlement Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement and the Exhibits
thereto are hereby incorporated herein by reference.
II. Applicable Rule Provisions:
Statutes 25th edition, effective 21st November 2023 (the “Statutes”).
General Regulations 24th edition, 1 January 2020, updates effective 1 January 2024.
(the “GRs”) updates effective 1 January 2024 (the “GRs”).
FEI Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations ("EADCMRs"), 3rd edition, 1
January 2021, updates effective 1 January 2023.
Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 3rd Edition, 1 February 2025 (“the IRs”).
III. PARTIES
4. Ms Kaitlin Campbell, (FEI ID 10060519), the PR in accordance with Article 118.3 of the GRs, is
an Athlete in the discipline of Jumping for the United States of America (the “USA”), who
competed with the Horse at the Event.
2

5. The FEI is the IOC-recognised international governing body for the equestrian sport
disciplines of Dressage and Para-Equestrian Dressage, Jumping, Eventing, Driving and Para-
Driving, Endurance and Vaulting.
IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND
6. The Horse was tested during the Event and returned positive results for Synephrine,
Octopamine and Dexamethasone.
7. Synephrine is classified as an Atypical Finding (“ATF”) substance under the FEI Atypical Findings
Policy (the “ATF Policy”). As such, the PR was first invited to provide an explanation for the
Synephrine finding to be considered by the ATF Panel.
8. Octopamine is classified as a Banned Substance and Dexamethasone is classified as a
Controlled Medication Substance under the FEI Equine Prohibited Substances List (the “List”).
The PR was informed that the proceedings relating to these findings would be notified once the
ATF proceedings in relation to Synephrine had concluded.
9. On 11 March 2025, the PR provided an explanation to the ATF Panel regarding Synephrine. The
PR submitted that the source was teff hay. On 7 May 2025, the FEI notified the PR that the ATF
Panel had accepted that the PR had proven that the source of the Synephrine was teff hay and
had thus closed the case in relation to Synephrine with no consequences. By the same letter,
the FEI informed the PR that she would receive “further notification from the FEI in relation to
the finding of Octopamine and Dexamethasone”.
10. By Notification Letter dated 16 June 2025 (the “Notification Letter”), the FEI informed the PR of
a potential violation of Articles 2.1 and 2.2 of the EADCMRs based on the findings for
Octopamine and Dexamethasone in the Sample. The PR was also notified in said letter that she
was provisionally suspended under Article 7.4.1 of the EADRs, and the Horse was also
provisionally suspended for two months until 15 August 2025.
11. In the Notification Letter, the FEI also explained to the PR that in accordance with Article 10.8.2
of the EADCMRs, if “the Person Responsible and/or member of the Support Personnel and/or
other Person admits an ECM/EAD Rule violation after being confronted with the ECM/EAD Rule
violation by the FEI and agrees to Consequences acceptable to the FEI” they may enter into a
Case Resolution Agreement and agree to Consequences acceptable at the sole discretion of
the FEI. The agreement shall be submitted to the FEI Tribunal (the “Tribunal”) for the sole
3

purpose of the Tribunal confirming that the criteria set forth in the EADCMRs have been fulfilled
(or do not apply) and, where so confirmed by the Tribunal, the final agreement shall state the
full reasons for any period of Ineligibility agreed, including (if applicable), a justification for why
the flexibility in sanction was applied.
12. On 5 September 2025, the PR requested the urgent lifting of the provisional suspension in
accordance with Article 7.4.4 (ii) of the EADR. The FEI consented to that request.
13. On 8 September 2025, the FEI Tribunal lifted the provisional suspension with effect
from midnight CET.
14. On 19 September 2025, the FEI submitted the Settlement Agreement with Exhibits for the
approval of the Tribunal and requested for a Panel to be appointed for the purpose or review
and approval of the said Settlement Agreement.
15. On 27 October 2025, the Tribunal informed the Parties of the appointment of a one person
hearing panel to adjudicate and approve this case. The Parties were asked to provide any
objections to the constitution of the hearing panel. On 27 October 2025, both the PR and
the FEI confirmed having no objections to the constitution of the hearing panel.
V. ACCEPTED TERMS
16. The Settlement Agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs, Article
10.8.2 of the ECMRs and is subject to the approval of the Tribunal.
NOW, THEREFORE, THE PARTIES HAVE AGREED TO THE FOLLOWING
TERMS FOR THE CLOSURE OF THE PROCEEDINGS:
17. In the matter related to the Sample, which was collected from the PR’s horse CASTLEFIELD
CORNELIOUS at the CSI5* MLSJ - Thermal CA (USA), on 7 December 2024, the PR, Ms Kaitlin
Campbell, and the FEI agree in accordance with 10.8.2 of the EADR and Article 10.8.2 of the
ECMR on the following:
a) The PR admits the violation of Article 2.1 (Presence of a Banned Substance in a Horse’s
Sample) and Article 2.2 (Use of a Banned Substance) of the EADR and Article 2.1
(Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a Horse’s Sample) and Article 2.2 (Use
of a Controlled Medication Substance) of the ECMR;
4

b) Pursuant to Article 10.9.5 of the EADR and Article 10.9.4 of the ECMR, the PR will be
considered to have committed one rule violation in respect of the Octopamine and
Dexamethasone findings, and the sanction will be based on the Banned Substance
(Octopamine);
c) The PR has established, on the balance of probabilities, how Octopamine entered the
Horse’s system;
d) The PR has established that she bore No Fault or Negligence for the Octopamine rule
violation in accordance with Article 10.5 of the EADR;
e) Therefore, no period of Ineligibility shall be imposed on the PR;
f) The results achieved by the PR and the Horse at the Event are disqualified, with all
resulting consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes, in
accordance with Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the EADR;
g) The PR shall not incur any fine;
h) No other sanctions will apply in this case;
i) Each party will bear its own legal and other costs incurred in connection with
these proceedings;
j) In accordance with Article 10.9.2 of the EADR and Article 10.9.2 of the ECMR, the Rule
Violation shall not be considered a prior violation for the purpose of Article 10.9 (Multiple
Violations) of the EADR or ECMR.
18. This agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR and Article 10.8.2 of
the ECMR and is subject to the approval of the FEI Tribunal. The Parties hereby kindly request
that the FEI Tribunal issue a Decision incorporating the terms of this agreement.
19. In accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR and Article 10.8.2 of the ECMR, the FEI’s
decision to enter or not enter into a case resolution agreement, and the amount of the
reduction to, and the starting date of, the otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility and the
confirmation of the case resolution agreement by the FEI Tribunal are not subject to appeal
under Article 13 of the EADR or Article 12 of the ECMR.
5

20. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADR and Article 13.3
of the ECMR, the Decision will be made public by the FEI.
21. The terms set out in this agreement have been agreed as a full and final settlement of all
claims relating to the subject matter of these proceedings. Accordingly, any and all other
claims for relief that any Party might otherwise have made against another in relation to the
subject-matter of these proceedings are released and discharged unconditionally, and they
may not be pursued in any form hereafter.
VI. DECISION
22. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, the EADCMRs, Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member of the USA-NF, which
is a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the EADRs and ECMRs.
23. Having reviewed the case summary, the full reasoning of the Settlement Agreement and the
Accepted Terms, the Hearing Panel accepts that the FEI found that the PR had established,
on a balance of probabilities, how Octopamine entered the Horse’s system.
24. The Tribunal further acknowledges that the PR and the FEI have agreed on the terms for the
closure of the proceedings, in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs, as detailed under
Section V of this Decision.
25. The Tribunal confirms that the Accepted Terms of the Settlement Agreement comply with
the EADRs and ECMRs and finds no grounds to object thereto.
26. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADRs and Article
13.3 of the ECMRs, this Final Decision will be made public by the FEI. The terms set out in the
Settlement Agreement are a full and final settlement of all claims relating to the subject
matter of these proceedings.
27. The Settlement Agreement and this Decision are not subject to appeal under Article 13 of
the EADRs or Article 12 of the ECMRs.
DECISION TO BE FORWARDED TO:
a. The Parties: Yes
6

b. The NF of the PR: Yes
c. Any other: No
